fields.meta_title: Review Request Automation for Every Customer | Emergent
fields.meta_description: See review request automation built four ways: a paid-invoice trigger, one reminder, skip rules, and a weekly board of requests and clicks.
fields.h1: Build Review Request Automation That Asks Every Customer
fields.hero_description: Get review request automation that emails every customer after a paid job and sends one reminder if the link goes unclicked.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Review Request App
fields.features_subheading: Each paid job starts one request, every customer gets the same review link, and the owner sees the week's numbers on one board.
fields.feature_1:
A request flow written as a sentence

Describe the flow as you would brief a new office manager: a day after the invoice is paid, email the customer. Emergent builds the app from that prompt, and a new one edits it.
fields.feature_2:
Triggers from the tools that close the job

The app connects to any tool with an API. A paid invoice in your billing software can start the request, and the job record supplies the customer's name and the technician's.
fields.feature_3:
The same link for every customer

Every customer the skip rules allow gets one public review link. Those rules read the job record, never a rating: a two-star customer gets the same email as a five-star one.
fields.feature_4:
One reminder, then silence

A customer who has not clicked by day 3 gets one reminder with the same review link. The request closes on day 7, and the customer hears nothing more about that job from you.
fields.feature_5:
A board the owner reads on Monday

A live dashboard counts the week's paid jobs, requests sent, skips, and review link clicks for each technician. Every request and its status sit in a database that you own.
fields.feature_6:
No task cap in a busy season

A spring rush sends more requests, and there is no task cap to hit. On paid plans the full code exports to your GitHub repository, and the free tier covers building and publishing.

fields.usecase_heading: Review Requests at One Plumbing Company
fields.tab_content_1:
24 hours after the invoice is paid, the request goes out

At 4:15 p.m. on Tuesday, the invoice for Odalys Brennan-Achebe's water heater install at Tamarack Lane Plumbing is marked paid. The app waits 24 hours, then emails her a request that names the job and her technician, Priya Castellanos. The email has one Leave a review button, the same public link every customer gets.
fields.tab_content_2:
By day 3 with no click, the app sends one reminder and stops

Three days pass with no click on Odalys Brennan-Achebe's request. On day 3 the app sends one reminder with the same Leave a review button, and the request log shows Reminder sent. That is the last email about the job: on day 7 the request closes whether she clicks or not, with no third email.
fields.tab_content_3:
Canceled on arrival or asked 40 days ago: no request

Two of Thursday's paid jobs get no request. Bram Ellery-Nwosu paid the trip fee but canceled his drain call when the technician arrived, and a job with no work done has nothing to review. Marisol Teague was asked about a faucet repair 40 days ago, inside the 90-day limit. Neither rule checks a rating.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 38 paid jobs last week, 36 got a request

Every Monday, the owner, Wendell Okafor-Lindqvist, opens the board for the week before. It shows 38 paid invoices, 36 requests sent, 2 skipped, and 14 clicks on the review link. By technician, Priya Castellanos's 15 requests drew 7 clicks, and Desmond Achterberg's 21 drew the other 7.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Review Request Automation
fields.howto_description: These 7 steps set up review request automation that asks each customer once, at a fixed time after the job, with one reminder.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the event that ends a job
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose one event in your billing or field service tool that marks a finished job, such as an invoice marked paid. One trigger per job keeps a customer from getting two requests for the same work.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Copy the public review link for each location from the review site and open it on a phone to test it. Store it on the location's record, and every request from that branch carries it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The FTC's guide for marketers says to know the rules of the platforms and websites on which those reviews may appear before you ask people for reviews. Read the policy of every site your link points to.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Send requests from the address on your invoices, with your business name in the sender line. A request from an unfamiliar address is easy to ignore, and a reply to it should reach a real person.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Keep ratings out of every rule
fields.howto_step_5_des: Base each skip on the job record, such as a canceled job or a recent ask, never on a satisfaction score. Every customer who passes the rules gets the same public review link.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Test with your own team first
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run ten test jobs with staff email addresses as the customers. Check that each email names the right technician, and that a canceled test job sends nothing at all.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Each week, subtract the skips from paid invoices and compare the result with requests sent. A gap means the trigger missed jobs: change it with a prompt before the next week starts.

faq_plan.a: Review request automation is a workflow that asks a customer for a review after a set event, such as a paid invoice or a closed job. No one sends the message by hand: it waits a fixed time after that event, sends the request, and logs whether the customer clicked the link.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up review request automation?
faq_plan.a: Describe the flow in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder: the event that starts it, the wait, and the jobs to skip. Emergent builds the app and its logic from that description. Connect the tool that marks jobs paid through its API, then run ten test requests addressed to your own team before a customer gets one.

faq_plan.q: Should review request automation skip customers who gave a low satisfaction score?
faq_plan.a: No. Google's policy for content on Maps says merchants may not discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers. The FTC, in its review guide for marketers, adds: don't ask for reviews only from customers you think will leave positive ones. Skip only for reasons the job record shows, and send everyone else the same link.

faq_plan.q: Should review request automation use the same email list as my newsletter?
faq_plan.a: Keep them apart. A review request is a one-to-one message about one finished job, sent once, while a newsletter goes to the whole list on a schedule. Trigger the request from the job record and leave the monthly send to newsletter automation. A review question tucked into a newsletter reaches people who never had a job done.

faq_plan.q: How long should review request automation wait after a job is done?
faq_plan.a: Long enough for the customer to have used the work, and short enough that they still remember the technician. A day suits a repair, while a remodel may need a week or two before the customer has lived with it. Emergent builds the wait from a plain-English prompt, and a new prompt changes it if clicks drop.

faq_plan.q: How many reminders should review request automation send?
faq_plan.a: One. Send it a few days after the first email, with the same link, then close the request. A customer who has ignored two emails about the same job has answered, and a third reads as pressure. The app logs each reminder beside the first email in the request history.

faq_plan.q: Can review request automation include a summary of the job?
faq_plan.a: Yes, keep it to two lines pulled from the job record: what was done and who did it. Attach nothing, because a file makes the email longer to load and the button harder to find. If customers also need the invoice as a file, pdf automation can generate it from the same job record and send it on its own.

faq_plan.q: What should a review request automation email say?
faq_plan.a: It should name the job, the technician, and the date, then ask one question with one button. For example: Thanks for having Priya out on Tuesday. How did the water heater install go? Leave out coupons and star pickers, and anything else that asks the customer to decide something before they reach the review page.

faq_plan.q: How should review request automation handle a business with several locations?
faq_plan.a: Give each location its own review link, and point every request at the page for the branch that did the job, read from the location on the job record. A review left on the wrong branch's page describes work that branch never did. In an app built on Emergent, every location's link and every request sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should review request automation wait for the final invoice on a large job?
faq_plan.a: Yes. On a job billed in stages, a request sent at the first payment reaches a customer whose work is half done. The quote at the start of the job belongs to proposal automation, and the review request belongs at the end, once the last invoice is paid.
